mil7.3.7:1.1: “Venerable Nagasena, when you said ‘one part of a well is to be grasped,’ what is that one part that is to be grasped?”
mil7.3.7:1.2: “Just as, Great King, a well holds a rope, a rein, and an ornament;
mil7.3.7:1.3: so too, Great King, one must be a yogin who practices yoga, endowed with mindfulness and situational awareness: going up and coming down, looking out and looking back, drawn in and extended, wearing the cloth patched from planks and leaves, having eaten, drunk, sucked on, and slept, having reached the top of the ladder and standing and sitting, sleeping and waking and talking, in a state of equipoise, acting with situational awareness.
mil7.3.7:1.4: This, Great King, is one part of a well that is to be grasped.
mil7.3.7:1.5: Thus spoken by the Blessed One, god among goddesses: ‘Mendicants, a mendicant should live mindful and aware; this is my instruction to you.’”
